```java
if (request == null || !StringUtils.hasText(request.text) || !StringUtils.hasText(request.sourceLanguage)
```

But the JsonPropertyDescription says default is zh for source and en for target, and they're `required = false`. This means when the LLM doesn't provide sourceLanguage or targetLanguage, the request will have null values, and apply returns null. This is a behavior contradiction - the description says defaults exist, but the validation rejects null.

The convenience constructor `Request(String text)` sets defaults, but that's not what the LLM uses via JSON deserialization. When deserialized from JSON with only `text`, the sourceLanguage and targetLanguage will be null, and the multi-arg canonical constructor is used, so no defaults applied.

This is a real bug: the "default is zh/en" documented behavior is not implemented for JSON deserialization path. The apply() will return null instead of using defaults.
